title: RhythmWeave
tagline: Turn rhythmic patterns into reproducible vector art.
inspiration: A generative artwork can be both expressive and reproducible when its visual form comes from a small, explicit recipe.
whatItDoes: Transforms pulse counts, ring settings and a palette into deterministic rhythm-based SVG artwork. Users can export the accessible vector and its recipe, then reproduce the composition.
howItWasBuilt: TypeScript implements the bounded pattern generator and validated SVG output. Next.js provides direct manipulation controls. PostgreSQL supports owned, expiring saved recipes.
technicalEvidence: Vercel hosting and the configuration endpoint respond successfully. Local tests and production builds pass. Database persistence and the complete connected workflow remain unverified; required credentials and submission artifacts are still pending.
authorship: Prepared with ChatGPT/Codex assistance. Shared Next.js/workspace infrastructure originates in code-up-matrix/axios-fx-compliance-agent; the product module was developed on 27 October 2026. Shared code must be disclosed under the event’s reuse rules.
eligibility: Art and technology fit. Overview says students only; body/rules say broader eligibility. Resolve conflict and prepare the Jan 3 presentation.
judgeAccessInstructions: Provide the private judging access code through the submission portal after live verification. Do not put it in public source.
challenges: The generator needs consistent pulse counts, deterministic output and safe exported markup across its supported parameter range.
accomplishments: Six standalone tests and the production build pass. The tests cover supported pulse counts, reproducibility and absence of script content; audience impact has not been measured.
lessons: A saved recipe provides a useful bridge between mathematical structure, artistic variation and reproducibility.
next: Resolve the event eligibility conflict, verify the deployed saving flow and prepare the required presentation using original compositions.
judgeFit: Connects mathematical rhythm and interactive visual art with an exportable artifact. The student eligibility conflict and presentation requirement remain open.
